en.headline: Wan Chai Sikh temple lights up in blue for Bandi Chhor Divas until 24 November
en.dek: Khalsa Diwan Sikh Temple on Queen's Road East is illuminated nightly with cascading blue lights to mark the festival, drawing residents and photographers.
body: The historic Khalsa Diwan Sikh Temple in Wan Chai has been covered in cascading blue lights to mark Bandi Chhor Divas and the concurrent Diwali period.

The display, which temple staff said runs from about 6:30pm to 9:30pm or 10pm each night, will continue until 24 November. Founded in 1901, the gurdwara at the junction of Queen's Road East and Stubbs Road is Hong Kong's oldest and only Sikh temple. The lights highlight its white facade, domes and arched details.

Temple representatives welcomed visitors, noting that those entering should dress modestly, remove their shoes and cover their heads in accordance with Sikh customs. The illumination has drawn crowds of residents and photographers in recent evenings.

zh.headline: 灣仔錫克教廟亮起藍燈慶祝囚徒解放日 至11月24日
zh.dek: 位於皇后大道東的Khalsa Diwan錫克教廟每晚以藍色燈飾點亮外牆，慶祝Bandi Chhor Divas及排燈節，吸引市民及攝影愛好者到場。
body: 灣仔歷史悠久的錫克教廟近日大規模掛起藍色燈飾，慶祝錫克教的囚徒解放日（Bandi Chhor Divas）及同期的排燈節。
廟方表示，燈飾每晚約六時半至九時半或十時亮起，將持續至11月24日。這座建於1901年的廟宇是本港最古老及唯一的錫克教廟，位於皇后大道東與司徒拔道交界。藍色燈光突出其白色外牆、圓頂及拱形設計。
廟方歡迎市民參觀，但須遵守錫克教習俗，衣著端莊、脫鞋及遮蓋頭部。連日來燈光吸引不少居民及龍友到場拍照。
